title: Podcast EP376: Samtec's Recent Pariticpaion in High-Profile Shows with Matt Burns
gist: In a SemiWiki podcast, Samtec's Matt Burns discusses the company's presence at the AI Infra Summit and ECOC, its copper and optical interconnect capabilities for AI systems, how complex it is to implement 400G, and Samtec's work on the Open CPX MSA initiative to standardize co-packaged optical engines.

insights.claim: According to Samtec's Matt Burns, the interconnect industry and its ecosystem are changing as AI grows and dominates the conversation. Samtec presents its support for both copper and optical interconnect as the way it enables next-generation solutions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Interconnect vendors are framing AI infrastructure as their main growth driver and hedging across copper and optics.
insights.quote: He describes some of Samtec’s unique capabilities to support both copper and optical interconnect to enable next generation solutions.
insights.locator: Daniel focuses on the recent shows

insights.claim: Matt Burns argues that implementing 400G links is complex enough that it needs collaboration across the ecosystem, not single-vendor solutions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Moving to 400G per lane will depend on multi-vendor interoperability, which favors firms active in standards bodies.
insights.quote: Matt describes the complexity of implementing 400G and the requirements for collaboration across the ecosystem.

insights.claim: Samtec is working on the Open CPX MSA initiative to standardize co-packaged optical engines, and Burns expects such initiatives to open a new wave of innovation.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A multi-source agreement for co-packaged optical engines could speed CPO adoption in AI switches and accelerators.
